html:
The plunder of Rome in June 455 by the Vandals under their king Gaiseric, who sailed from their kingdom in Africa.

The trigger was a broken marriage deal. The murder of Valentinian III in 455 put Petronius Maximus on the throne, and he married his son to the princess who had been promised to Gaiseric's son. Gaiseric came with a fleet. Maximus fled and was killed by a Roman mob. Pope Leo I met Gaiseric and is said to have got him to spare the people from killing and burning.

For two weeks the Vandals stripped the city of its treasures, including, by one account, spoils of the Temple of Jerusalem that Titus had brought to Rome after the destruction of 70. They took thousands of captives to Carthage, among them the empress Eudoxia and her daughters. The sack, worse than the Visigoth sack of 410, later gave us the word "vandalism".
sum: The plunder of Rome in June 455 by the Vandals under their king Gaiseric, who sailed from their kingdom in Africa.
